t: Count Number of Rectangles Containing Each Point
o: Rectangle i covers point (x,y) iff li ≥ x and hi ≥ y. Naively checking all rectangles per point is O(nq) = 2.5e9 — too slow. Crucially, heights are capped at 100 while coordinates reach 1e9, which suggests bucketing by height. Example 1: point (2,1) fits rectangles with h≥1 and l≥2 → two; point (1,4) needs h≥4, l≥1 → one.
k: Heights are ≤ 100, so grouping rectangles by height makes per-point scans over at most 100 buckets feasible.
Within each height bucket, sort the widths and binary-search to count widths ≥ x.
The fully general solution processes points offline in decreasing y with a Fenwick tree over compressed widths.

a.n: Approach 1: Bucket by Height + Binary Search
a.i: Store, for each height h, the sorted list of widths of rectangles with that height. A point (x,y) is covered by every rectangle with height ≥ y and width ≥ x, so sum, over h from y to 100, the count of widths ≥ x via bisect.
s: Group rectangle widths by height; sort each group.
For each point (x,y), iterate h = y..100 and add (bucket length − index of first width ≥ x).
a.t: O(q · 100 · log n) — each point scans ≤ 100 sorted buckets with binary searches.

a.i: Sort points by y descending and rectangles by height descending. Sweep rectangles in, inserting each width into a Fenwick tree indexed by compressed width; when reaching a point's y, the tree contains exactly rectangles with h ≥ y, and a suffix-count query gives widths ≥ x.
s: Compress all widths; sort rectangles by height desc and points by y desc.
Pointer-sweep rectangles into the BIT as y decreases.
For each point, answer = (inserted so far) − prefix count of widths < x.
a.t: O((n + q) log(n + q)) — sorting plus BIT operations dominate.
a.sp: O(n + q) for the BIT and ordering arrays.

w: Approach 1 is the intended sweet spot given h ≤ 100; Approach 2 generalizes to arbitrary heights. Pitfalls: points on edges count (use ≥ comparisons carefully — count widths ≥ x, not > x), and don't forget heights equal to y. Follow-up: report which rectangles contain each point, or handle dynamic insertions.
